findings.title: Runtime-hardening test does not constrain writable mounts
findings.what: The check named `cache as the only writable app mount` merely looks for the cache volume line. It never parses the service volume list or rejects additional read-write mounts. The immutable baseline already contains a second intentional writable adoption-store mount and the test still prints this assertion as passing, proving that an arbitrary future writable mount would evade the least-privilege guard.
findings.fix: Parse the app service volume entries and assert an explicit allowlist of writable destinations, including the currently intentional cache and adoption-store paths; require every other bind or volume mount to be read-only and reject unknown writable destinations.
findings.acceptance: A fixture matching the current two approved writable destinations passes; adding an arbitrary `/host:/app/extra:rw` mount fails; removing `:ro` from either Claude data source mount also fails; the assertion text names the actual allowlist.
findings.verifyNote: The baseline assertion at lines 67-68 is a single presence regex. Running the baseline test printed that the cache was the only writable app mount even though a direct inspection of the same app service showed the deliberate adoption-store read-write mount, reproducing the false security guarantee.
